title: Best-fit probabilistic models of deterministic data look more random than the data

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Best-fit probabilistic models of deterministic data look more random than the data

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When probabilistic models such as block-frequency, Markov or probabilistic cellular automaton models are fitted to data generated by deterministic cellular automata, they reproduce the statistics used in fitting but their typical behavior is considerably more random and misses most detailed features of the data.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In most cases, the typical behavior produced by the model looks considerably more random than the data.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Statistical Analysis” (from p. 588), p. 592. Scope: statistical modeling of data generated by deterministic simple programs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The specified models and deterministic generators make a direct, inexpensive replication possible. The unrestricted prevalence statement remains conditional on choices of rules, fitting criteria, and feature metrics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate data from a preregistered set of deterministic cellular automata, fit block-frequency, Markov, and probabilistic-CA models, and compare held-out higher-order statistics and visual structure. Greater entropy and loss of detailed features in most fitted samples would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visual randomness needs quantitative metrics.

Most-cases prevalence depends on the sampled rule distribution.

'Best fit' depends on model order and objective.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.82
data existence: 1.0

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model classes and the data source are fully specified, and both fitting and resampling are standard. Agreement on the fitted statistics together with a loss of detailed structure is a direct confirming pattern; reproduction of those details is a direct refutation. The check is a computation on generated data, not a new experiment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit block-frequency, Markov, and probabilistic cellular-automaton models to data from deterministic cellular automata, matching the statistics used in the fit, then compare typical model samples with the original on features not in the fit. Samples that match the fitted statistics but are more random and miss the detailed features confirm the claim; samples that reproduce those features refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A probabilistic model with enough hidden state can be made to copy the data, so the model class has to stay the ones named.

'More random' needs a pre-registered feature score beyond the fitted statistics.
